spec.description: Shows whether plex-exporter can reach your Plex Media Server, who is streaming and how, and how busy the host is. The Libraries and Streaming history tabs go deeper, and the host panels show only for a server with Plex Pass.

spec.title: Server status
spec.description: Shows whether plex-exporter reached your Plex server on its last check, a few seconds ago. Online is normal. Unreachable means Plex is down, restarting or rejecting the token, and the other panels stop updating. Exporter not scraped means no metrics arrive at all, so check the exporter container and your scrape job.

spec.title: Library sizes
spec.description: Items, disk space and total length per library, largest first, with totals in the footer. Use it to see which library takes the most space. Items refresh every 15 minutes, and disk space and length every minute. No libraries yet means plex-exporter has not read the library list.

spec.title: Session poll
spec.description: Shows whether the last read of current playback worked. plex-exporter reads it every 5 seconds. Reachable is normal. Unreachable while Server status reads Online means only that request fails, so Active sessions and the stream counts are out of date.

spec.title: Active sessions
spec.description: One row per stream that is playing, paused or stopped in the last minute, longest first. Stream shows how Plex delivers it. Direct play sends the file as it is, direct stream repackages it and transcode converts it, which costs the most CPU. Location shows whether the player connects from your network or over the internet.

spec.title: Session bandwidth
spec.description: Network bandwidth Plex reports for all streams together, per server. Compare it with your upload speed when remote streams buffer. It reads 0 when nobody is streaming, and a gap means plex-exporter was not scraped.

spec.title: Session bitrate
spec.description: The bitrate of the media being streamed, added up across all streams, per server. A high value points to large files, such as 4K remuxes, that strain your upload or your players. It reads 0 when nobody is streaming, and a gap means plex-exporter was not scraped.

spec.title: Active transcodes
spec.description: Streams Plex is converting right now on the selected servers, because the player cannot play the file as it is. Transcoding uses the most CPU, so a high count explains a slow server. The tile turns yellow at 1 transcode and orange at 3, and zero is normal when your players support your files. Unknown means plex-exporter has not identified the server yet.

spec.title: Host CPU
spec.description: CPU use of the whole machine Plex runs on, from Plex's own statistics. A yellow dashed line marks 80% and a red one marks 90%. Sustained use above 80% slows transcodes and library scans, and above 90% streams can stutter. An empty panel means Plex reported no host statistics for the selected servers.

spec.title: Host memory
spec.description: Memory use of the whole machine Plex runs on, from Plex's own statistics. A yellow dashed line marks 80% and a red one marks 90%. Use above 80% leaves little room for new streams, and sustained use above 90% risks slowdowns and failed transcodes. An empty panel means Plex reported no host statistics for the selected servers.

spec.title: Plex version
spec.description: The Plex Media Server version running now. Use it to confirm that an update went through. Unknown means plex-exporter has not identified the server yet, which happens for a few seconds after it starts or while Plex is unreachable.

spec.title: Active streams
spec.description: Streams playing or paused right now on the selected servers, with the trend over the time range. A stream drops out about a minute after it stops. The colour turns yellow at 1 stream, orange at 3 and red at 5, because each stream uses upload bandwidth and server time. Unknown means plex-exporter has not identified the server yet.

spec.title: Plex Pass
spec.description: Shows whether each selected server's owner account has Plex Pass. Host CPU and host memory need it, so the Host resources row shows only for a server with Plex Pass and No explains why it is missing. Unknown means plex-exporter has not identified the server yet.

spec.expr: max by (server) (plex_server_info{server=~"$server",plex_pass="true"}) or on (server) (0 * max by (server) (plex_server_info{server=~"$server"}))

spec.title: Total items
spec.description: Movies, episodes, tracks and photos across the selected libraries, added together. plex-exporter counts them every 15 minutes, so the number can lag after a large scan. Not counted yet means the first count since plex-exporter started has not finished.

spec.title: Total storage
spec.description: Disk space the selected libraries use, as Plex reports it. Compare it with the free space on your media drives. Unknown means plex-exporter has not read the library list yet.

spec.title: Total duration
spec.description: How long it would take to play everything in the selected libraries back to back. It grows when you add media and drops when you remove it. Unknown means plex-exporter has not read the library list yet.

spec.title: Library change per day
spec.description: Items added minus items removed in each library, per day. A bar below zero means items were removed. A deleted or emptied library shows no bar, because plex-exporter stops reporting a library once it holds no items. Bars follow the dashboard zoom but never get narrower than one day, and today's bar appears once it has two samples.

spec.title: Items by content type
spec.description: Movies, episodes, tracks and photos across the selected servers, counted from every library of that type. Use it to see what your collection is mostly made of. No libraries yet means plex-exporter has not counted the items.

spec.title: Average length per item
spec.description: Total running time of each library divided by its item count, so a show library gives the average episode length. A photo library has no running time and reads 0. A library with no items is left out.

spec.title: Average size per item
spec.description: Disk space of each library divided by its item count. A high average in a movie library usually means many 4K or remux files. A library with no items is left out.

spec.title: Storage change in this range
spec.description: How much disk space each library gained over the selected time range, estimated from the first and last reading. A negative bar means files were removed or replaced by smaller ones. Pick a longer range in the time picker to see slow growth.

spec.title: Plays by delivery
spec.description: Streams playing at each moment, split by how Plex delivers them. Direct play sends the file as it is, direct stream repackages it without re-encoding, and transcode re-encodes it on the server. A large transcode share means devices or bandwidth limits force conversions, so check the Active sessions table for which ones. Unknown counts streams Plex reported with no delivery decision or with one this exporter does not recognise, so the stack always adds up to every active stream.

spec.title: Plays by network
spec.description: Streams playing at each moment, split by whether the player is on your home network or connects from outside. Remote plays use your upload bandwidth, so a rise there explains slow remote streams. The line sits at 0 while nobody is watching. Unknown counts streams Plex reported with no network location or with one this exporter does not recognise, so the stack always adds up to every active stream.

spec.title: Watch time by user
spec.description: Time each user spent playing in the selected range, longest first. Times are estimates from plex-exporter's 5-second session check, and history reaches back only as far as your Prometheus keeps metrics. Each stream can lose up to one scrape interval, so short streams count low or are missed. No watch time in this range means nothing played, or plex-exporter was not scraped.

defaults.noValue: No watch time in this range

spec.title: Watch time by library
spec.description: Time spent playing from each library in the selected range, longest first. Times are estimates from plex-exporter's 5-second session check, and history reaches back only as far as your Prometheus keeps metrics. Each stream can lose up to one scrape interval, so short streams count low or are missed. No watch time in this range means nothing played, or plex-exporter was not scraped.

defaults.noValue: No watch time in this range

spec.title: Most watched titles
spec.description: The 20 titles played longest in the selected range, with the show, season and episode for TV and the artist, album and track for music. Times are estimates from plex-exporter's 5-second session check, and history reaches back only as far as your Prometheus keeps metrics. Each stream can lose up to one scrape interval, so short streams count low or are missed. No plays in this range means nothing played, or plex-exporter was not scraped.

spec.title: Bandwidth by network
spec.description: Bandwidth Plex reports for the streams playing at each moment, split by home network and remote players. When remote streams buffer, compare the Remote band with your upload speed. Unknown covers streams with no network location or one this exporter does not recognise, so the stack adds up to all streams. The lines sit at 0 while nobody is streaming, and a gap means plex-exporter was not scraped.

spec.title: Plex Media Server

spec.name: server
spec.label: Server
spec.description: The Plex servers to show, by the name each server reports. All adds every server together.
